issues.description: The problem statement and tests expect a function named simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) but the template msd.py defines simulate_one_round(...) (different name). Additionally, the template's plot_msd calls simulate_msd_one_round(...) even though only simulate_one_round is present. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the template will have missing symbol errors or confusion about which function to implement. The solution repository implements simulate_msd_one_round, resolving the mismatch, but the template is inconsistent with the specification and its own plotting helper.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement and tests by renaming the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round with the expected signature (n_shots: int, p: float), or add a wrapper simulate_msd_one_round that delegates to simulate_one_round. Also ensure plot_msd and other helpers call the same function name.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a function named simulate_msd_one_round, but the template repository defines it as simulate_one_round. This inconsistency can confuse students when mapping the required API (from the problem) to the starter code and may cause tests or example usage (which expect simulate_msd_one_round) to fail or be difficult to locate.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round to match the problem statement and solution (or add a thin wrapper simulate_msd_one_round that calls simulate_one_round). Ensure all references (e.g., in plot_msd) use the consistent name simulate_msd_one_round.
